text: Then the LORD appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
From the belly of the fish Jonah prayed to the LORD his God:
"In my distress I called to the LORD, and he answered me. From the belly of Sheol I cried for help, and you heard my voice.

versions.text: "In my distress I called to the LORD, and he answered me. From the depths of the grave I cried for help, and you heard my voice.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads 'from the belly (beten) of Sheol,' deliberately echoing 'the belly of the fish' in v. 1–2. 'Depths of the grave' loses this striking verbal link, which is one of the poem's central images and carries well in oral reading. A footnote could explain Sheol as the realm of the dead.

text: You hurled me into the deep, into the heart of the seas, and the currents swirled around me; all your breakers and your waves swept over me.
I said, 'I have been driven from your sight; yet I will look again toward your holy temple.'
The waters closed in over me, threatening my life; the deep surrounded me; seaweed was wrapped around my head.
I sank down to the roots of the mountains; the earth barred me in forever. But you brought my life up from the pit, O LORD my God.
As my life was ebbing away, I remembered the LORD, and my prayer came to you, to your holy temple.
Those who cling to worthless idols forsake the steadfast love that would be theirs.

versions.text: Those who cling to worthless idols forfeit the grace that could be theirs.
versions.explanation: Hebrew 'chesed' here is God's covenant loyalty; 'grace' imports a slightly different theological register, and 'forfeit... that could be theirs' is wordy for oral reading. 'Steadfast love' renders chesed more precisely while keeping the line rhythmic.

text: But I will sacrifice to you with a voice of thanksgiving. What I have vowed I will fulfill. Salvation belongs to the LORD!"

versions.text: But I, with a song of thanksgiving, will sacrifice to you. What I have vowed I will fulfill. Salvation belongs to the LORD!"
versions.explanation: The interrupting phrase 'But I, with a song of thanksgiving,' breaks the flow when read aloud; moving the prepositional phrase after the verb reads more naturally. 'Voice' also matches the Hebrew 'qol' more closely than 'song.'

text: And the LORD commanded the fish, and it vomited Jonah out onto dry land.
